title: Google Cloud launches two new AI chips to compete with Nvidia
description: Google's newest TPUs are faster and cheaper than the previous versions. But the company is still embracing Nvidia in its cloud — for now.
author: Julie Bort

title: Google turns Chrome into an AI co-worker for the workplace
description: Google brings Gemini-powered "auto browse" capabilities to Chrome for enterprise users, letting workers automate tasks like research, data entry, and more.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Google makes an interesting choice with its new agent-building tool for enterprises
description: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform takes an interesting approach: It is geared for IT and technical users.
author: Julie Bort

title: AI Overviews are coming to your Gmail at work
description: The AI Overviews will offer instant summaries pulled from across multiple emails.
author: Sarah Perez

title: OpenAI teams up with Infosys to bring AI tools to more businesses
description: Infosys said the integration will be used to help its clients modernize software development, automate workflows, and deploy AI systems, initially focusing software engineering, legacy modernization, and DevOps.
author: Jagmeet Singh

title: AI is spitting out more potential drugs than ever. This start-up wants to figure out which ones matter.
description: 10x Science has raised a $4.8 million seed round to help pharmaceutical researchers understand complex molecules.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Exclusive: Google deepens Thinking Machines Lab ties with new multi-billion-dollar deal
description: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab has signed a multi-billion-dollar deal with Google Cloud for AI infrastructure powered by Nvidia's latest GB300 chips, TechCrunch has exclusively learned.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Google Maps is about to get a big dose of AI
description: Generative AI is being infused into Google's popular feature within Maps.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: The most interesting startups showcased at Google Cloud Next 2026
description: Google wants AI startups on its cloud and has showcased a long list of them at its annual conference.
author: Julie Bort

title: Meta will record employees’ keystrokes and use it to train its AI models
description: Meta says that it has a new internal tool that is converting mouse movements and button clicks into data that can train its AI models.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Unauthorized group has gained access to Anthropic’s exclusive cyber tool Mythos, report claims
description: Anthropic told TechCrunch it is investigating the claims, but maintains that there is no evidence that its systems have been impacted.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: SpaceX is working with Cursor and has an option to buy the startup for $60B
description: The move could shore up weaknesses at each company, but it also reveals them. Neither Cursor nor xAI has proprietary models that can match the leading offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI — the same companies now competing directly with Cursor for the developer market.
author: Tim Fernholz
